title: Djisktra's Algorithm
problemStatement: Single-source shortest paths on a weighted graph with non-negative edge weights. Return dist[0…n-1] (∞ / −1 for unreachable).
intuition: Greedily settle the closest unsettled node (BFS with a min-heap instead of FIFO). Needs non-negative weights. Negatives → use Bellman-Ford (a different algorithm, not a “brute” Dijkstra).

approaches.title: Brute: O(n²) Dijkstra (scan for min each time)
approaches.idea: Same greedy: repeatedly pick the unsettled node with smallest dist by scanning an array — no heap. Correct, slow on sparse graphs.
limitations: Not Bellman-Ford — that is for negatives / cycle detect

approaches.title: Optimal: Dijkstra with min-heap
approaches.idea: dist[], heap of (d,u); skip stale entries (d != dist[u]).
approaches.time: O((n + m) log n) with binary heap
approaches.dryRun: Settle nodes in increasing distance order; once popped with dist[u], it is final (non-negative weights).
approaches.whyWorks: Non-negative weights ⇒ no future path can improve a settled node.
limitations: Negative edge → WRONG — use Bellman-Ford instead

python.notes: Skip stale heap entries with d != dist[u].

specialTechnique.title: Algorithm choice table
specialTechnique.body:
Unweighted → BFS
Non-negative weights → Dijkstra
Negative edges / neg-cycle detect → Bellman-Ford (optimal for that problem — not “brute force”)
0/1 weights → 0-1 BFS
DAG → topo + relax
All-pairs → Floyd-Warshall (dense) / Dijkstra from each (sparse, w≥0)

commonMistakes: Labeling Bellman-Ford as brute force for this problem
followUps: K shortest paths / constraints on stops?
interviewInsight: State the weight assumption before coding. If negatives appear, switch algorithms — don’t call Bellman-Ford a brute.
